div.l: Vpon̄ a book alwey in cloistre and poure
Or swinke with his handes in laboure
And Austyn hou shall the world be serued
Late Austyn haue his labour to him reserued
Therfore he was a pricasour a right
Greyhoundes he had as swifte as foul of fliȝt
Of Priking and of hunting for the hare
Was al his lust for no cost wold he spare
I sauȝ his sleues purfiled at the hand
With grys and that the fynest of the londe
And for to fasten the hood vnder the chyn̄
He had of gold wrouȝt a full curious pyn̄
A loue in the gretter ende ther was
His hed was balled and shon as glas
And eke his face as it had ben enoynte
He was a lord full fat and in good point
His yhen stepe and rolling in his hed
That stemed as a forneis of a Led
His bootes souple his hors in gret estat
Now certainli he was a faire prelat
He was nat pale as a for pined gost
A fat swan loued he best of any roste
His Palfrey was as broun as any berie
A frere ther was a wantoıı̄un ⁊and a merie
A lymitour a full solempne man̄
In all the ordres foure ther is non þᵗat can
So mochell of daliaunce and faire language
He had made many a faire mariage
Of yong wommen̄ of his ougne coste
Vnto his ordre he was a noble poste
Full welbeloued and familier was he
With frankeleines oueral in his contre
And eke with worthi men of eueri toun̄
For he had power of confessioıı̄un
As he seid him self more than the curatt
For of his ordre he was licenciat
Full swetly herd he confessioıı̄un
And plesaunt was his absolucioıı̄un
He was an esi man to yiue penaunce
There as he wist to haue a good petaunce
For vnto a poore ordre for to yiue
Is a signe that a man is well Ishriue
And if he yaf he durst make avaunt
He wist that a man was repentaunt
For many a man so harde is of his herte
He may nat wepe al thouȝ he sore smerte
Therfore in stede of weping and praiers
Men mot yeue siluer vnto poore freris
And certainli pinnes for to yiue faire wyfes
His tipet was ay farsed full of knifes
And certainli he had a mery note
Wel coude he synge and pleyen on the rote
Of tidinges he bar vtterli the pris
His necke white as any flour delys
Therto as strong was as any champioıı̄un
He knew the tauernes wel in eueri toun̄
And eueri hosteler and tapstere
Rather than a beggere or a Lazer
For vnto such a worthi man as he
Accordeth nat as be his faculte
To haue with such Lazers aqueintaunce
It is nat honest it may nat avaunce
For to dele with no such poraill
But alle with riche and sellers of vitaill
And ouer all ther as proufit shuld arise
Curteis he was and louli of seruice
Ther was noman nowher so vertuous
He was the best begger in his hous
And yaf a certain ferme for the graunt
Non of his bretheren cam there in his haunt
For thouȝ a widewe had but a shoo
So plesant was his In principio
Yet wolde he haue a ferthing or he went
His purchas was welbetter than his rent
And rage he coude as it were a whelpe
In Louedayes coude he mochel helpe
For he ne was like no cloistrer
With thredebare cope as is a poore scoler
But he was like a maister or a Pope
Of double worsted was his semy cope
That round as was a belle out of a presse
Somwhat he lipsed for his wantounesse
To make his englissh swete vpon his tonge
And in harping whan that he had songe
His yhen twinkeled in his hed ariȝt
As don theȝ sterres in the frosty niȝt
This Lymytour was I cleped Huberd
A Marchaunt ther was with a forked berd
In motley and high on hors he sat
Vpon his hed a flaundrissh beuer hatt
His bootes clapsed faire and fetisly
His resons he spak ful solemply
